content: Granuloma faciale (GF) is a rare, benign, chronic dermatological condition of unknown etiology. It is characterized by the presence of one or more cutaneous nodules, which most commonly appear on the face. In some cases, lesions may also develop on areas of the skin outside the face, particularly in regions exposed to sunlight. The condition was first identified as a distinct clinical entity in 1950 by Lever and Leeper. In the same year, the term granuloma faciale was proposed by Pinkus and his colleagues to describe this disorder.
